column1: # Severity drives the response, not just the sort order:
#   CRITICAL - credential that grants access if live. Triggers the halt
#   HIGH     - credential-shaped and usually real, but scope varies.
#   MEDIUM   - generic assignment. High false-positive rate by design; the
#              cost of missing a real key exceeds the cost of triage.
#   INFO     - public by design. Present so they are recognised and NOT
#              reported as leaks. A publishable key filed as a breach burns
#              client trust and buries the findings that matter.
# No leading \b: real config is camelCase (apiSecret, clientSecret, authToken)
# and a word boundary before "secret" never matches inside "apiSecret".
